name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.194.0 — Corrects two stale prose claims: the sketch command no longer says the session ratifies a surface approval (only the approval made on the mock page advances it), and the roadmap-overview template no longer claims the mock viewer composes the journey graph from roadmap surfaces blocks (SEED parses those blocks into the mock app journeys.ts). 7.193.0 — Git-ignored path derivation is now one shared library (spec/scripts/lib/ignored-paths.js) used by both repo walks — scope-reconcile's at-risk walk and red-check's wildcard tests-row expansion — so a wildcard File Plan row no longer resolves test files inside git-ignored checkouts; an exact-path row is still resolved wherever it points, and a wildcard that expands to zero files now raises a warning instead of passing in silence. 7.192.0 — The build driver's already-DONE refusal now covers both admission branches instead of only the implementing resume. A spec whose closed document was reverted to hardened — the shape a stale blob committed from another session produces — used to walk straight past the ledger check, and the hardened branch's own writes flipped status and stamped diff_base at a HEAD that already contained the shipped work, so red-check's pre-image and the dirty-path check were satisfied by construction and the rebuild proceeded blind. The refusal now runs before any write on either path, and names the reverted status, the git log -S command that finds the close commit, and superseded as the only route to a deliberate rebuild.
